how_these_heads_influence_orders.mark: MEASURED from code and the live audit; the conclusions are INFERRED from those
how_these_heads_influence_orders.channel_1_vol_hard_gate: src/runtime/intents.py regime hard gate. With REGIME_ML_VERDICT_MODE=use (ROADMAP M16 says it has been live for BTC since 2026-06-28; I did not read the VM env this session), the advisory head's vol label replaces the frozen label, and config/regime_policy.yaml::trend_vol OFF-cells may DROP an intent. The effect only reduces trading: an intent is dropped only when vol_enforced = vol_gated AND the label is ML-sourced. A frozen-fallback label never enforces. So demoting a head REMOVES blocks and can never block anything new.

The per-strategy advisory_policy defaults to 'annotate' (logs only, no resize). grep -rn advisory_policy config/ returned 0 lines (the same grep for trend_vol returns config/regime_policy.yaml, so the probe works), so I read this as annotate-only: no order effect.

But no trend_vol OFF-cell names a SOL strategy (the cells name trend_donchian, ict_scalp_5m and squeeze_breakout_4h). The probe is shown to work: the same query on BTCUSDT returns 213 rows. So the E72 premise that it is 'ADVISORY, so it influences orders' does not hold for SOL.

model_verdicts.verdict_detail: The demote case does NOT hold on today's evidence. The drift is real and persistent: drift_clean has failed on two consecutive days. But every regime-appropriate capability gate passes. The 0-for-8 turns out to be every real-money BTC trade since the log starts, and the model did not cause any of them. Demoting would remove the 16 blocks the head made on OFF-cells that were written up as money-losing, and would stop none of the 8 losses. Per drift-remediation, an interim demote is only for a head that is 'actively harmful now', and none of today's evidence shows harm. Route the drift to diagnosis, not to demotion.

live_discrimination.axis_caveat: ml/promotion/stage_guard.py::_demote_triggers suppresses brier_lift and AUC as demote triggers for regime heads, because the regime score against trade win is the WRONG AXIS (MB-20260630-001). The score is top-class confidence, whatever the class. brier_lift=-0.84 against baseline_brier=0.0 is arithmetic from an all-loss sample (0.8403 = mean(score^2) at win=0), not a calibration finding. Stage-guard's own demote reason today is drift only.

zero_for_eight_rederived.rows: 6x ict_scalp_5m (2 short, 4 long) and 2x trend_donchian long, all bybit_2. pnl -5.51, -5.50, -3.19, -2.75, -4.26, -4.05, -3.98, -0.83 (sum -30.06 USD). Exits: 6 sl, 2 reconciler_filled. The reconciler closes are a separate health-review item and are not scored here.
zero_for_eight_rederived.did_the_model_cause_them: No. The join is time window plus symbol. It records that the head SCORED BTC while each trade was open. It does not record that the head acted on that trade. The head's only real-money path (channel 1) can only DROP intents, and a frozen-fallback label never enforces a vol drop. So with the head demoted, all 8 would still have been taken. At each entry the head's label (regime_ml_vol_shadow row at the same minute) was 'calm' in 8 of 8. The frozen label was 'volatile' in 6 of 8 (5312, 5369, 5409, 5429, 5591, 5675). The most the model can be charged with is NOT blocking these: a 'volatile' label in a trending or chop regime would have dropped them under the current OFF-cells. I did not retrieve the trend regime at entry (regime_shadow_gate returned 0 rows for this window), so I cannot say which of the 8 a 'volatile' label would have blocked.
zero_for_eight_rederived.weight: Weak evidence against the model: n=8, on the wrong axis per the code, and made of trades it did not cause. If anything it bears on whether the head should block MORE, which demotion makes impossible.
